name: GitHub Pages
tagline: Static hosting straight from a public GitHub repo.
description: Serves static sites (HTML, CSS, JS) from a GitHub repository, with custom domains and HTTPS. Ideal for docs, portfolios and SPA builds. No server code runs here.
restrictions: Not allowed as free hosting to run an online business, e-commerce site or commercial SaaS (GitHub Pages limits page).
Private repositories need a paid GitHub plan for Pages.
One user or organization site per account; deployments time out after 10 minutes.
pros: Pairs with GitHub Actions for custom builds
Soft limits instead of surprise bills

name: Cloudflare Pages
tagline: Static and JAMstack hosting with unlimited bandwidth.
description: Git-connected hosting for static sites and frontend frameworks on the Cloudflare network. The free plan advertises unlimited sites, static requests and bandwidth, with a monthly build budget.
restrictions: 500 builds per month, 1 build at a time.
Commercial use terms not stated on the pricing page.
pros: Same account as Workers, D1, R2
cons: Server logic means moving to Workers

name: Netlify
tagline: Frontend hosting with a shared monthly credit pool.
description: Git-based deploys, previews, serverless functions and forms. The free plan runs on a 300 credit monthly pool shared between deploys, compute, bandwidth, forms and requests.
restrictions: If a project exceeds its limits, all projects on the account pause until the next billing cycle.
Limited to 1 free member.
pros: Hard monthly limits: no surprise costs
cons: One over-limit project pauses all of them

name: Vercel (Hobby)
tagline: Frontend cloud with functions, tuned for Next.js.
description: Deploys frontend frameworks with serverless functions, image optimization and previews. The Hobby plan is free with monthly included usage and no option to buy more.
restrictions: Hobby accounts are limited to the usage caps and cannot purchase additional usage.
When a limit is exceeded you usually wait 30 days before using the feature again.
Commercial use on Hobby: not stated on the pricing or Hobby plan pages. Check the Terms of Service.
cons: 30-day lockout when a cap is hit

name: Render (Free instances)
tagline: Free web services, Postgres and Key Value with sleep mode.
description: Hosts web services, background workers and databases from Git. Free instances exist for web services, Postgres and Key Value, with spin-down and expiry rules.
restrictions: Free web services spin down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic; spin-up takes about one minute.
Free Postgres expires 30 days after creation (14-day grace period), 1 GB fixed storage.
One free Postgres and one free Key Value per workspace. Key Value data is in-memory and lost on restart.
cons: Overage billed if a payment method exists

name: Cloudflare Workers
tagline: Serverless functions at the edge, 100k requests per day.
description: Runs JavaScript, TypeScript and WebAssembly on Cloudflare's network. The free plan includes daily request quotas plus free allowances for KV and Durable Objects.
restrictions: 10 ms CPU time per invocation on the free plan.
KV free: 100,000 reads/day, 1,000 writes/day, 1 GB stored. Daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC.
pros: Same account as D1, R2, Workers AI
cons: Edge runtime is not full Node.js

name: Cloudflare D1
tagline: Serverless SQLite database for Workers.
description: SQLite-based database bound to Cloudflare Workers. The free plan covers millions of row reads per day and 5 GB of total storage.
restrictions: 10 databases on the free plan.
Daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC.

name: Cloudflare R2
tagline: S3-compatible object storage with a free monthly quota.
description: Object storage for files, images and backups with an S3-compatible API. Free usage includes 10 GB-month of storage plus millions of operations.
restrictions: Free: 10 GB-month storage, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations per month.
pros: Works from Workers or any backend

name: Cloudflare Free (DNS, CDN, SSL)
tagline: Free SSL, CDN and DDoS protection for your domain.
description: Point your domain at Cloudflare to get a CDN, free SSL certificates and DDoS protection on the free plan.
restrictions: DNS specifics are not described on the free plan page.
You need your own domain (not free).

name: Supabase
tagline: Postgres, auth, storage and edge functions in one project.
description: Hosted Postgres with authentication, file storage, realtime and edge functions. The platform is open source and can also be self-hosted.
restrictions: Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity.
Limit of 2 active free projects.
Credit card requirement not stated on the pricing page.

name: Neon
tagline: Serverless Postgres that scales to zero.
description: Managed serverless Postgres with branching, autoscaling and scale to zero. The permanent free plan allows up to 100 projects.
restrictions: 1 GB storage per project, 20 GB total across projects.
Scales to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity (cannot be turned off on Free).
pros: Pay-as-you-go next step with no monthly minimum
cons: Cold start after scale to zero

name: Turso
tagline: Edge SQLite (libSQL) with 100 free databases.
description: Hosted SQLite built on libSQL with replication and embedded replicas. The free plan is generous on reads and databases.
restrictions: 10 million rows written per month on Free.
gem: Jarvis likes it: 100 databases on free, 500M monthly row reads, no card. Gary immediately made 99 side projects.

name: MongoDB Atlas (M0)
tagline: Free forever shared MongoDB cluster.
description: Managed MongoDB document database. The M0 shared cluster is listed as free forever with 512 MB of storage.
restrictions: Up to 100 operations per second.
Shared RAM and vCPU; 32 MB sort memory.
Connection limit and card requirement not stated on the pricing page.

name: Firebase (Spark)
tagline: Google's app backend: Firestore, Auth, Hosting.
description: Backend-as-a-service with Firestore, authentication and hosting. The Spark plan needs no payment method but excludes Cloud Functions and Cloud Storage.
restrictions: Cloud Functions and Cloud Storage are not available on Spark.
Hosting transfer: 360 MB per day.
Phone auth not applicable on Spark.

name: Upstash Redis
tagline: Serverless Redis billed per command.
description: HTTP and TCP accessible Redis for serverless and edge apps. Free plan covers 500K commands per month.
restrictions: 1 free database, 250 MB data.
Entering a credit card upgrades the database to pay-as-you-go.
pros: Works over HTTP from edge runtimes

name: Oracle Cloud Always Free
tagline: Always Free VMs (Arm and AMD), card required.
description: Oracle Cloud offers Always Free compute (Arm Ampere A1 and AMD), block storage and more, plus a time-limited trial credit. Exact Always Free capacities are not shown on the landing page.
restrictions: Credit or debit card required for identity verification (no prepaid or virtual cards).
US$300 trial credit for 30 days is separate from Always Free and only in select countries.
Exact Always Free quotas: see Oracle docs (not verified here).
notes: Always Free quantities need verification against the Oracle Free Tier docs.

name: Deno Deploy
tagline: Serverless JS/TS with KV. Sunset announced for April 2027.
description: Serverless platform for Deno and TypeScript with built-in KV. The free plan targets personal and small projects.
restrictions: The pricing page states Deno Deploy will be sunset in April 2027.
Free plan is for personal use and smaller projects.
cons: Announced sunset: do not start long-lived projects here

name: Cloudflare Tunnel
tagline: Expose a local or private server without opening ports.
description: The cloudflared connector links a machine to Cloudflare without a public IP. Quick Tunnels (TryCloudflare) give a temporary URL for testing.
restrictions: Quick Tunnels are for testing and development only, with a hard limit of 200 in-flight requests.
Pricing for named tunnels is not stated on the pages checked.
pros: Great for demoing a local app
gem: Gary hosts prod on his laptop through a quick tunnel. Jarvis reminds him the docs say testing only.

name: Tailscale (Personal)
tagline: Private mesh VPN between your devices.
description: WireGuard-based network connecting your machines securely. The Personal plan is free for up to 6 users but limited to non-commercial use.
restrictions: Personal plan is only suitable for non-commercial use.
Up to 6 users, 50 tagged resources.

name: Coolify
tagline: Self-hosted Heroku/Netlify alternative for your own server.
description: Open source platform to deploy apps, databases and services on your own servers with a web UI. Free when self-hosted; you pay for the server.
restrictions: Needs a server you operate.

name: React
tagline: The UI library most of the web runs on.
description: Component-based JavaScript library for building user interfaces, maintained by Meta and the community.

name: Vite
tagline: Fast dev server and bundler for modern frontends.
description: Frontend build tool with instant dev server and optimized production builds. Supports React, Vue, Svelte and more.

name: Astro
tagline: Content-first web framework shipping zero JS by default.
description: Web framework for content sites, blogs and landing pages that renders to static HTML and adds interactivity only where needed.

name: Svelte
tagline: Compiler-based UI framework with tiny bundles.
description: UI framework that compiles components to efficient JavaScript at build time.

name: Tailwind CSS
tagline: Utility-first CSS framework.
description: CSS framework built from utility classes, generating only the styles you use.

name: shadcn/ui
tagline: Copy-paste React components you own.
description: Collection of accessible React components that you copy into your project instead of installing as a dependency.

name: Vitest
tagline: Vite-native unit test runner.
description: Fast unit test framework sharing Vite's config and transforms, with a Jest-compatible API.

name: Playwright
tagline: End-to-end browser testing across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit.
description: Browser automation and end-to-end testing framework from Microsoft.

name: VSCodium
tagline: VS Code binaries without Microsoft telemetry.
description: Community-built, freely licensed binaries of the VS Code editor source.

name: Hoppscotch
tagline: Open source API client in the browser.
description: Lightweight API development tool for REST, GraphQL and WebSocket requests. Usable in the browser or self-hosted.
gem: A Postman-style client that opens in a browser tab. Jarvis approves of anything that does not need a 400 MB install.

name: GitHub Actions
tagline: CI/CD and cron jobs, free on public repos.
description: Workflow automation for builds, tests, deploys and scheduled jobs. Standard runners are free for public repositories.
restrictions: Free on standard runners for public repos. Private repos on GitHub Free get $12 of compute per month (2,000 CI/CD minutes per the pricing page).
500 MB artifact storage shared with Packages; 10 GB cache per repo.
Larger runners are always billed.

name: GitHub Codespaces
tagline: Cloud dev environments, monthly free hours for personal accounts.
description: Browser or VS Code connected dev containers hosted by GitHub. Personal free accounts get included compute time and storage each month.
restrictions: 120 hours compute and 15 GB-month storage per month on personal GitHub Free. Usage multiplier depends on machine size.
Included hours apply to personal accounts, not free organizations.

name: Better Auth
tagline: TypeScript auth library you run in your own backend.
description: Framework-agnostic authentication library for TypeScript with email/password, OAuth and plugins. Stores users in your own database.
pros: Your data stays in your DB

name: Clerk (Hobby)
tagline: Drop-in auth UI and user management.
description: Hosted authentication with prebuilt sign-in components, sessions and organizations. Free Hobby plan up to 50,000 monthly retained users per app.
restrictions: Clerk branding cannot be removed on Hobby.
Fixed 7-day session lifetime; no MFA, passkeys or SMS codes on Hobby.
Up to 3 dashboard seats.

name: PocketBase
tagline: Backend in one file: SQLite, auth, files, realtime.
description: Open source backend packaged as a single executable with an embedded SQLite database, auth, file storage, realtime and an admin UI.
pros: One binary, runs on a laptop or tiny VPS
cons: Needs somewhere to run 24/7 in prod
gem: A whole backend in one file. Gary ran it from his Downloads folder. Jarvis moved it to a server.

name: Appwrite (self-hosted)
tagline: Open source backend server: auth, DB, storage, functions.
description: Self-hostable backend platform with databases, authentication, storage and functions, deployed with Docker.
notes: Appwrite also sells a hosted cloud; its free tier was not verified here.

name: discord.js
tagline: Node.js library for Discord bots.
description: Library for interacting with the Discord API from Node.js, the standard choice for JavaScript Discord bots.
restrictions: A gateway bot needs an always-on Node.js process.

name: Godot Engine
tagline: Free open source 2D and 3D game engine.
description: Complete game engine with editor, scripting (GDScript, C#) and exports to desktop, mobile and web. No royalties.

name: Phaser
tagline: HTML5 game framework for 2D browser games.
description: JavaScript/TypeScript framework for 2D games rendered with WebGL or Canvas in the browser.

name: Groq API
tagline: Very fast LLM inference with a free plan.
description: API for open-weight LLMs on Groq hardware. A free plan exists with per-model rate limits per minute and per day.
restrictions: Example free limits (openai/gpt-oss-120b): 30 requests/min, 1,000 requests/day, 8K tokens/min, 200K tokens/day.
The rate-limit page does not clearly separate Free and Developer plan figures.
notes: Rate limit table labelling is ambiguous on the source page.

name: Google Gemini API (free tier)
tagline: Free tier on several Gemini models; prompts may train Google products.
description: Google's Gemini API offers a free tier on many models, including Flash and Flash-Lite variants and embeddings. Free tier content is used to improve Google products.
restrictions: Free tier: content is used to improve Google products (paid tier: not used).
Image, video and music models (Imagen, Veo, Lyria) have no free tier.
Free tier rate limits are on a separate page (not captured here).
cons: Do not send sensitive data on free tier

name: OpenRouter (free models)
tagline: One API, many models, including :free variants.
description: Unified API routing to many LLM providers. Models with the :free suffix cost nothing within daily request limits.
restrictions: Free models: 20 requests/minute; 50 requests/day if fewer than 10 credits purchased, 1,000/day after buying at least 10.

name: Cloudflare Workers AI
tagline: Run models on Cloudflare GPUs, 10,000 neurons per day free.
description: Serverless inference for text, image, speech and embedding models from Workers. Usage is measured in neurons.
restrictions: 10,000 neurons per day free on both Workers Free and Paid. Beyond that requires Workers Paid.
Neurons per request depend on the model.

name: Hugging Face
tagline: Models, datasets and free CPU Spaces.
description: Hub for open models and datasets, with Spaces to host ML demos. Free accounts can run Spaces on CPU Basic hardware.
restrictions: Free Spaces run on CPU Basic (2 vCPU, 16 GB memory).
Free-account inference credits are not stated on the pricing page (PRO lists $2/month).

name: Ollama
tagline: Run open LLMs locally with one command.
description: Runs open-weight language models on your own machine with a simple CLI and a local API. Local use is free and unlimited.
restrictions: Running models on your own hardware is unlimited. Cloud models are billed per token.
Speed depends on your hardware.

name: llama.cpp
tagline: The C/C++ engine behind local LLMs.
description: High-performance LLM inference in C/C++ for CPUs and GPUs, with a built-in server. Powers many local AI tools.
gem: The engine under half the local AI tools you know. Jarvis respects anything that runs on a toaster.

name: whisper.cpp
tagline: Local speech-to-text, no API bill.
description: Port of OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model in C/C++, running fully offline on CPU or GPU.
gem: Transcribe podcasts on your own machine. Infrastructure: $0. Electricity: Gary does not want to talk about it.

name: Open WebUI
tagline: Self-hosted ChatGPT-style interface for local and API models.
description: Web interface for chatting with Ollama or OpenAI-compatible APIs, with RAG and multi-user features. Self-hosted.
license: Open WebUI License (BSD-3 style with additional branding terms)
restrictions: Custom license with extra clauses on top of BSD-3 terms: read it before rebranding or redistributing.
pros: Polished UI over your own models
cons: License is not a standard OSI license
notes: openSource and commercialUse left unknown pending a full license review.

name: Qdrant
tagline: Vector database, open source with a free cloud cluster.
description: Vector similarity search engine for embeddings and RAG. Open source for self-hosting, plus a free managed cluster.
restrictions: Free cloud cluster: single node, 0.5 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 4 GB disk, no high availability.

name: Chroma
tagline: Embeddable open source vector database.
description: AI-native embedding database that runs in-process or as a server, popular for local RAG prototypes.

name: pgvector
tagline: Vector search inside Postgres.
description: Postgres extension adding vector types and similarity search, so embeddings live next to your relational data.
restrictions: Your Postgres host must offer the extension.

name: GitHub Copilot Free
tagline: AI code completions in your editor, monthly cap.
description: Free tier of GitHub's AI coding assistant, for vibe coding sessions with a monthly completion allowance.
restrictions: Up to 2,000 completions per month. Chat request limit not stated on the pricing page.

name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
tagline: Free, cookie-free web analytics via a JS beacon.
description: Privacy-focused analytics that does not use cookies or localStorage. Works with a JavaScript beacon, no need to proxy your site.
restrictions: No usage limits stated on the product page.
pros: $0, no cookie banner needed for it

name: Umami
tagline: Open source analytics: free cloud hobby plan or self-host.
description: Simple privacy-focused web analytics. Use the Umami Cloud Hobby plan or self-host it for free.
restrictions: Cloud Hobby: up to 100K events/month, 1 website, 6 month retention.
Self-hosting is always free (you pay the server).
cons: Cloud free plan covers one site

name: GoatCounter
tagline: Tiny open source analytics, free for reasonable public use.
description: Lightweight web analytics without cookies or persistent personal data, run by an independent developer. Hosted for free within reasonable use, or self-hosted.
restrictions: Free hosted service for reasonable public usage; millions of pageviews per day is not appropriate.
No monthly cap number published.
gem: An indie, one-person analytics tool that has been quietly doing its job for years. Jarvis finds it suspiciously reasonable.

name: Plausible Community Edition
tagline: Self-hosted privacy analytics (AGPL).
description: Self-hosted edition of Plausible Analytics. Free to run on your own infrastructure under AGPL-3.0.
restrictions: AGPL: modifications you serve to users must be shared.
cons: Needs a server and a database

name: Resend
tagline: Developer email API, 3,000 emails per month free.
description: Transactional email API with React Email support and a clean developer experience.
restrictions: 3,000 emails per month, 100 per day, 3 domains, 30-day data retention.

name: Brevo (Free)
tagline: Email marketing and transactional, 300 emails per day.
description: Email marketing and transactional platform. The free plan sends up to 300 emails per day once the account is approved.
restrictions: Up to 300 emails per day after account approval.
Removing the Brevo logo appears to be a paid feature (not confirmed on the page).
pros: SMTP relay usable by other tools

name: listmonk
tagline: Self-hosted newsletter and mailing list manager.
description: High-performance, self-hosted newsletter manager in a single binary with Postgres. Sends through any SMTP relay.
restrictions: Needs an SMTP provider to actually deliver email.
gem: Newsletter software with no per-subscriber bill. Gary will finally email his 3 followers at scale.

name: Sentry (Developer)
tagline: Error tracking and tracing, free for one user.
description: Application monitoring for errors, performance tracing and session replay. The Developer plan is free for a single user.
restrictions: 1 user, 5k errors, 5M spans, 50 replays, 1 cron monitor, 1 uptime monitor, 30-day lookback.
The page does not say whether the 5k errors are per month.

name: UptimeRobot (Free)
tagline: 50 uptime monitors at 5-minute intervals.
description: Website and API uptime monitoring with alerts and a basic status page. Free plan allows commercial use.
restrictions: 50 monitors, 5 minute interval, 1 basic status page.

name: Uptime Kuma
tagline: Self-hosted uptime monitor with status pages.
description: Self-hosted monitoring tool for HTTP, TCP, ping and more, with notifications and status pages.
restrictions: Monitoring from the same server as your app hides outages of that server.
gem: Unlimited monitors on a $0 Docker container. Gary monitors his monitors.

name: n8n (Community Edition)
tagline: Workflow automation, self-hosted, fair-code license.
description: Node-based workflow automation with hundreds of integrations. The self-hosted Community edition is free under the Sustainable Use License.
restrictions: License: use only for your own internal business purposes or non-commercial/personal use; redistribute only free of charge for non-commercial purposes.
Files marked .ee need an Enterprise license.
cons: Not open source by OSI definition

name: Meilisearch
tagline: Fast typo-tolerant search engine you can self-host.
description: Search engine with instant, typo-tolerant results and a simple REST API. Core is MIT; some enterprise features are under BUSL.
restrictions: Enterprise Edition features are under the Business Source License 1.1.
pros: Great relevance out of the box

name: Lucide
tagline: Clean open source icon set with framework packages.
description: Community-maintained icon library with packages for React, Vue, Svelte and plain SVG.

name: Penpot
tagline: Open source design and prototyping, Figma-like.
description: Web-based design and prototyping tool built on open standards (SVG), usable online or self-hosted.
notes: Hosted plan terms were not verified here.
gem: A design tool you can host yourself. Gary keeps his mockups next to his memes.

name: Excalidraw
tagline: Hand-drawn style whiteboard, open source.
description: Virtual whiteboard for sketching diagrams with a hand-drawn look. Works in the browser without an account.
gem: Architecture diagrams that look like Gary drew them, which is the point.

name: Unsplash
tagline: Free photos under the Unsplash License.
description: Photo library usable for free, including commercially, without permission. Attribution is appreciated but not required.
restrictions: The license does not allow compiling Unsplash images to build a similar or competing service.

name: Open-Meteo
tagline: Weather API with no key for non-commercial use.
description: Open weather forecast and historical API built on national weather services data. Free tier for non-commercial use, data under CC BY 4.0.
restrictions: Free tier is non-commercial.
600 calls/min, 5,000/hour, 10,000/day, 300,000/month.
Attribution required (CC BY 4.0).
cons: Commercial use needs a paid plan
gem: Weather data without signing up for anything. Jarvis notes: non-commercial only, Gary.

name: OpenStreetMap standard tiles
tagline: The community map tiles, under a strict usage policy.
description: Map tiles served by the OpenStreetMap Foundation. Fine for light use with proper attribution; heavy use should go elsewhere.
restrictions: Visible attribution required.
Bulk downloading, prefetching and offline use are prohibited.
Send a clear, unique User-Agent. Best-effort service, no SLA.

name: CoinGecko API (Demo)
tagline: Crypto prices and market data, free demo plan.
description: Crypto market data API covering prices, market caps and exchanges. A free Demo plan exists with limited endpoints and rate limits.
restrictions: The API page presents the Public API as recommended for hobbyists, not for production or commercial use.
Free plan quotas and attribution rules not captured: the pricing page could not be fetched during verification.

name: Vue
tagline: Progressive framework for web UIs.
description: Approachable component framework with reactive templates, usable from a script tag up to full apps.

name: SvelteKit
tagline: Full-stack framework for Svelte.
description: Application framework for Svelte with routing, server rendering and adapters for static hosts, Node and edge runtimes.

name: Hono
tagline: Tiny web framework for every JS runtime.
description: Small, fast web framework built on Web Standards that runs on Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, Node and more.
pros: Same code on edge and Node
gem: An API framework that fits inside a Worker free tier. Jarvis likes small things that do their job.

name: Express
tagline: The classic minimal Node.js web framework.
description: Minimal and flexible Node.js web framework, the long-standing default for HTTP APIs.

name: Fastify
tagline: Fast, low-overhead Node.js web framework.
description: Web framework for Node.js focused on performance and a plugin architecture with schema-based validation.

name: Prisma ORM
tagline: Type-safe ORM for Node.js and TypeScript.
description: ORM with a declarative schema, migrations and a generated type-safe client for Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and more.
notes: Prisma also sells hosted products; only the open source ORM is listed here.

name: Drizzle ORM
tagline: Lightweight TypeScript ORM that feels like SQL.
description: Headless TypeScript ORM with SQL-like queries, works in serverless and edge runtimes.

name: TanStack Query
tagline: Async state and data fetching for UIs.
description: Library for fetching, caching and synchronizing server state in React, Vue, Svelte and Solid.

name: Docusaurus
tagline: Documentation sites from Markdown.
description: Static site generator for documentation with versioning, search integration and MDX.

name: VitePress
tagline: Fast static docs powered by Vite and Vue.
description: Static site generator designed for technical documentation, fast to build and to load.

name: Biome
tagline: One fast tool to format and lint JS/TS.
description: Formatter and linter for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON and CSS in a single fast binary.

name: Bruno
tagline: Offline-first API client, collections in Git.
description: Desktop API client that stores collections as plain files in your repository, with no cloud sync required.
gem: An API client that keeps your requests in Git instead of somebody's cloud. Jarvis: finally.
notes: Bruno also sells paid editions; the open source app is listed here.

name: act
tagline: Run GitHub Actions locally.
description: Runs your GitHub Actions workflows locally in containers for fast feedback before pushing.
gem: Test the workflow on your machine instead of pushing 14 commits named "fix ci". Gary has 14 such commits.

name: Mailpit
tagline: Catch and inspect emails during development.
description: Local SMTP server with a web UI that captures outgoing emails for testing, without sending them.

name: Keycloak
tagline: Self-hosted identity and access management.
description: Identity server with SSO, OAuth2/OpenID Connect, SAML, user federation and an admin console.

name: Gitea
tagline: Lightweight self-hosted Git service.
description: Self-hosted Git forge with issues, pull requests, packages and CI (Actions), packaged as a single binary.

name: Tabler Icons
tagline: 5,000+ free SVG icons.
description: Large set of consistent outline and filled SVG icons with packages for common frameworks.

name: Phosphor Icons
tagline: Flexible icon family with six weights.
description: Icon family available in thin, light, regular, bold, fill and duotone weights.

name: Inter
tagline: Open typeface designed for screens.
description: Sans-serif typeface built for user interfaces, with variable font support.

name: JetBrains Mono
tagline: Open monospace font for developers.
description: Monospaced typeface designed for reading code, with programming ligatures.

name: Squoosh
tagline: Image compression in the browser.
description: Web app that compresses and converts images (WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL) locally in the browser with side-by-side preview.
gem: Shrink images in a tab, nothing uploaded. Gary's 9 MB hero image is now 180 KB.

name: Mermaid
tagline: Diagrams from text, rendered in Markdown.
description: Generates flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts and more from a text syntax; supported in many Markdown tools.

name: daisyUI
tagline: Component classes for Tailwind CSS.
description: Tailwind CSS plugin adding semantic component classes and themes.

name: Radix Primitives
tagline: Unstyled accessible React components.
description: Low-level, accessible UI primitives for React that you style yourself.

name: Motion
tagline: Animation library for React and JS.
description: Production-ready animation library for JavaScript, React and Vue with gestures and layout animations.
notes: Motion also sells paid extras; the open source library is listed here.

name: Lottie Web
tagline: Render After Effects animations on the web.
description: Renders Lottie JSON animations exported from After Effects as SVG, canvas or HTML.

name: PixiJS
tagline: Fast 2D WebGL/WebGPU renderer.
description: 2D rendering engine for the web, used for games, interactive art and data visualizations.

name: three.js
tagline: The 3D library of the web.
description: JavaScript 3D library over WebGL and WebGPU for scenes, games and visual experiments.

name: p5.js
tagline: Creative coding for artists and beginners.
description: JavaScript library for creative coding with a focus on accessibility for artists, designers and educators.

name: FFmpeg
tagline: Convert, cut and stream any audio or video.
description: Command-line toolkit to record, convert and stream audio and video in almost any format.
restrictions: Enabling GPL parts at build time switches the license to GPL v2+.

name: yt-dlp
tagline: Command-line audio/video downloader.
description: Feature-rich command-line downloader for media from many sites.
restrictions: Downloading content may be restricted by the terms of the site and by copyright. You are responsible for what you download.

name: MapLibre GL JS
tagline: Open source interactive vector maps.
description: Library for interactive vector tile maps in the browser, community fork of Mapbox GL JS v1.
restrictions: You still need a tile source (self-hosted or a provider).

name: AppFlowy
tagline: Open source Notion alternative.
description: Workspace for docs, wikis and project boards that you can run locally or self-host.
notes: AppFlowy also sells cloud plans; only the open source app is listed.

name: Logseq
tagline: Local-first outliner and knowledge base.
description: Privacy-first knowledge management app working on plain Markdown and Org files on your disk.

name: Immich
tagline: Self-hosted photo and video backup.
description: Self-hosted Google Photos alternative with mobile backup, face recognition and sharing.

name: Vaultwarden
tagline: Lightweight Bitwarden-compatible server.
description: Unofficial Bitwarden-compatible password manager server written in Rust, light enough for small machines.
restrictions: Unofficial: not affiliated with Bitwarden. Securing and backing up the server is on you.

name: Plane
tagline: Open source project tracking (Jira/Linear style).
description: Project management with issues, cycles and modules; self-hostable.
notes: Plane sells cloud and commercial editions; the AGPL community edition is listed.

name: Stirling PDF
tagline: Self-hosted PDF toolbox.
description: Web app to merge, split, convert, compress, OCR and sign PDFs on your own server.
gem: Every PDF tool you pay for online, on your own box. Gary merged his tax PDFs. Jarvis is proud.
notes: Some enterprise features are paid; the MIT-licensed app is listed.

name: Paperless-ngx
tagline: Scan, OCR and archive your paperwork.
description: Document management system that OCRs, tags and indexes your scanned documents.

name: Syncthing
tagline: Peer-to-peer file sync, no cloud.
description: Continuous file synchronization between your devices, encrypted, with no central server.
gem: Dropbox without Dropbox. Your laptop and your phone talk directly.

name: LocalSend
tagline: AirDrop for every OS, on your local network.
description: Cross-platform app to send files between nearby devices over the local network, no internet or account needed.

name: ntfy
tagline: Push notifications via simple HTTP calls.
description: Send push notifications to your phone or desktop with a plain HTTP request; self-hostable.
gem: curl -d "deploy done" ntfy.sh/your-topic and your phone buzzes. Gary uses it for price alerts. Obviously.
notes: The hosted ntfy.sh service has its own plans, not verified here.

name: Activepieces
tagline: Open source Zapier alternative.
description: No-code automation builder with many integrations and AI pieces; community edition is MIT.
restrictions: Code under packages/ee is under a commercial license.

name: Node-RED
tagline: Flow-based automation for APIs and IoT.
description: Browser-based flow editor to wire APIs, devices and services together, runs on small hardware.

name: changedetection.io
tagline: Watch web pages and get alerts on changes.
description: Self-hosted website change monitoring with notifications, useful for price or terms tracking.
gem: Watches pricing pages for you. Free Stack plans to use exactly this kind of tool to catch free tier changes.
notes: A hosted paid version exists; self-hosted is listed.

name: NocoDB
tagline: Turn a database into a spreadsheet UI (Airtable style).
description: No-code platform that puts a spreadsheet interface and APIs on top of SQL databases.
license: Sustainable Use License (fair-code, not OSI, since 2026-01-29)
restrictions: License changed to the Sustainable Use License on 2026-01-29: check the terms before commercial or hosted use.
pros: Spreadsheet UI on your own DB

name: Jan
tagline: Desktop app to chat with local LLMs offline.
description: Open source ChatGPT-style desktop app that runs models locally, with an OpenAI-compatible local server.

name: ComfyUI
tagline: Node-based local image generation.
description: Modular graph interface for diffusion models to generate images and video on your own GPU.
restrictions: Needs a capable GPU for reasonable speed. Model licenses vary per model.

name: Continue
tagline: Open source AI code assistant for your IDE.
description: IDE extension for VS Code and JetBrains that connects any model, including local ones, for chat, edit and autocomplete.

name: Cline
tagline: Autonomous coding agent inside VS Code.
description: VS Code extension that plans and edits code, runs commands and uses MCP tools, with the model of your choice.
restrictions: The extension is free; model usage is billed by whichever provider you plug in (or free with local models).

name: Aider
tagline: AI pair programming in your terminal.
description: Command-line coding assistant that edits files in your Git repo and commits changes, works with many models.
restrictions: Model costs depend on the provider you use.

name: MCP reference servers
tagline: Official Model Context Protocol server examples.
description: Reference implementations of MCP servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory...) to plug tools into AI agents.
restrictions: Reference implementations, meant as examples: review before production use.

name: Transformers.js
tagline: Run ML models in the browser.
description: Runs Hugging Face models directly in the browser or Node with WebGPU/WASM, no server needed.
gem: Embeddings and small models running in the visitor's browser. Your server bill: still $0.

name: Tesseract OCR
tagline: Open source OCR engine, 100+ languages.
description: Optical character recognition engine with command-line tool and library bindings.

name: Piper
tagline: Fast local text-to-speech.
description: Neural text-to-speech system that runs locally, even on a Raspberry Pi.
restrictions: Voice model licenses vary per voice.
notes: Check the repository README for the current maintained location of the project.

name: LocalAI
tagline: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API.
description: Drop-in OpenAI API replacement that runs LLMs, image, audio and embedding models on your hardware.

name: PostHog (Free)
tagline: Product analytics, replay, flags: 1M events free each month.
description: Product analytics suite with session replay, feature flags, surveys and error tracking. The free plan is permanent and needs no credit card.
restrictions: Free each month: 1M analytics events, 5K session recordings, 1M feature flag requests, 1,500 survey responses, 100K exceptions.
On the free plan, extra events are permanently dropped and flags return a quota-limited response. Allowances do not roll over.
pros: No credit card, not a trial

name: Grafana Cloud (Free)
tagline: Metrics, logs and traces with 14-day retention.
description: Hosted observability stack (Prometheus metrics, Loki logs, Tempo traces, k6 load tests) with a free tier and no credit card.
restrictions: 10k active metric series, 50 GB logs, 50 GB traces, 50 GB profiles per month, 14-day retention.
500 k6 virtual user hours per month; 3 active users.

name: Better Stack (Free)
tagline: Uptime monitors, status page and logs for personal projects.
description: Uptime monitoring, incident alerts, status pages and log management. The free plan is labelled for personal projects.
restrictions: Labelled "free for personal projects".
10 monitors and heartbeats, 1 status page, 3 GB logs and 3 GB traces kept 3 days, 100,000 exceptions per month.
Check frequency on free not stated.

name: Backblaze B2
tagline: Object storage with 10 GB always free.
description: S3-compatible cloud object storage. The first 10 GB of storage are always free, with free egress up to 3x your average monthly storage.
restrictions: First 10 GB storage always free; egress free up to 3x average monthly storage, then $0.01/GB.
Storage beyond the free 10 GB: $6.95 per TB per month.

name: Pinecone (Starter)
tagline: Managed vector database, 2 GB free.
description: Serverless vector database for semantic search and RAG with a free Starter plan.
restrictions: Up to 2 GB storage, 1M read units and 2M write units per month, 5 indexes, 1 project, 2 users, 1 GB egress.
Usage past the monthly allowance is blocked until the next period or an upgrade.

name: Cloudinary (Free)
tagline: Image and video API with 25 monthly credits.
description: Media management with on-the-fly image transformations, optimization and CDN delivery. Free forever plan, no credit card.
restrictions: 25 credits per month; 1 credit = 1,000 transformations, or 1 GB storage, or 1 GB image bandwidth.
Video bandwidth credits are for paid plans only. 3 users, 1 account.

name: Cerebras Inference ($5 credit)
tagline: Fast LLM inference: one-time promo credit, card required.
description: High-speed inference API for open models. Free access is a one-time promotional credit after adding a payment method.
restrictions: Add a valid payment method to receive a one-time $5 promotional credit, which expires 30 days after activation.
Access pauses when the credit runs out or expires, unless you buy pay-as-you-go credits. You are not charged automatically.
notes: Free tier rate limits were not visible on the pricing page.

name: Cloudflare Turnstile
tagline: Free CAPTCHA alternative.
description: Privacy-friendly bot check that replaces CAPTCHAs with a snippet of code. Cloudflare describes it as free.
restrictions: Free plan limits (widgets, requests) not stated on the product page.
notes: Plan limits are in Cloudflare docs, not captured in this verification.
